pending_commit.commit_message: init: Create cgroup subdirectories for generic containers The existing cgroup subsystems are created and owned by root and therefore cannot be modified by processes running as non-root inside the containers. This creates a new subdirectory inside each of the cgroup subsystems and makes user-containers the owner of those directories. Then generic containers can create their own cgroups inside these subdirectories. BUG=none TEST=Boot CrOS and verify /sys/fs/cgroup/<subsys>/user_containers exists for all subsystems and all directories are owned by the user-containers user. Change-Id: Ib93505b25c9c058afb4d56a304c0f61f170d7511 Signed-off-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/367449 Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: clk: rockchip: optimize 800MHz and 1GHz pll rates on RK3399 Usually, the 800MHz and 1GHz are supplied for CPLL and NPLL in the RK3399. But dues to the carelessly copying from RK3036 when the RK3399 bringing up, the refdiv == 6, it will increase the lock time, and it is not an optimal configuration. Let's fix them for the lock time and jitter are lower: 800 MHz: - FVCO == 2.4 GHz, revdiv == 1. 1 GHz: - FVCO == 3 GHz, revdiv == 1. servo_glados_overlay: Add in servo_{v4,micro}_interface to raw_usbpd_uart_pty. servo_glados_overlay defines raw_usbpd_uart_pty on an interface specifically for servo v2/v3 (that is reworked) that is not compatible with servo v4/uServo. This is a sticky situation since this control really should belong in the servo v2/v3 overlay but at the same time doesnt since those controls don't really exist without a rework on the v2/v3. A proper solution is still being hashed out but this is blocking servod from starting which is blocking all boards that use this overlay from deploying. Right now just define a servo v4/uServo specific interface for this control so that servod can get going. It's expected that usbpd won't work this way but we're not using it as part of deployments and the majority of testing doesn't as well so we're ok with that. BUG=chromium:660922 TEST=Started servod with change with servo v4/uServo and asuka and did not see the conflict. CHROMIUM: supports a new dbus method ResetAdvertising This patch supports a new dbus method ResetAdvertising which removes all existing advertisements and resets the advertising intervals to default. Note that advertising would be disabled when the last advertisement is removed. CQ-DEPEND=CL:390172 BUG=chromium:602461 TEST=Perform the following steps on a DUT. On a terminal, use btmon to monitor the logs. $ btmon On another terminal, execute the following steps: 1. Copy example-advertisement to the DUT, and run the command on the DUT. $ ./example-advertisement & 2. Copy example-advertising-intervals to the DUT and run the command on the DUT. $ ./example-advertising-intervals --set 200 200 3. On another machine, use hcitool to observe advertising packets of the DUT. $ sudo hcitool lescan 4. Reset advertising on the DUT. $ ./example-advertising-intervals --reset Observe that advertisements are removed in the btmon log and advertising is disabled. CHROMIUM: drm/rockchip: Store vblank event in driver data Currently the IRQ handler accesses the CRTC state without taking necessary locks, which is generally incorrect, but also causes a race condition that allows next atomic commit overwrite the pending event with its own (possibly NULL). It is because vop_isr() calls drm_crtc_handle_vblank() before vop_handle_vblank(), which does the event signaling, so the thread waiting on drm_atomic_helper_wait_for_vblanks() might get woken up earlier than the event is signaled and it might let next commit proceed before the previous one is fully done (i.e. the event is signaled). This patch makes the driver store the event pointer in its private data, protected under drm->event_lock. Next commit is prevented from overwriting this pointer, because vop_crtc_atomic_flush() calls vop_wait_for_irq_handler() before it assigns the new event. Effectively, relevant code is brought to the state as it exists in upstream. BUG=chrome-os-partner:58763 TEST=passed 2960 iterations of suspend_stress_test (stopped due to unrelated issue) Change-Id: I77ce190eac360c460fe44cdf3dcf9aeb7d349567 Signed-off-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/385457 Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>
